transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
President Trump says he's rejecting a short-term plan offered by Iran to reopen the Strait
of Hormuz after seven days.
The proposed plan would also have temporarily ended the hostilities in order to restore
ceasefire talks with the U.S.
NPR's Emily Fang has more.
Iran had proposed the plan this week at the United Nations General Assembly meetings in
New York, a plan very similar to a memorandum of understanding that the two countries agreed
upon back in June.
And Iran's president told CBS News he'd allow UN nuclear inspectors into Iran if there
were a long-term ceasefire deal with the U.S.
But Trump wrote on True Social Saturday morning, "Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon," and
then told reporters before departing for Tennessee that the plan was "not acceptable."
Trump claimed Iran was negotiating out of a position of weakness and said they were "dying."
Emily Fang, NPR News, Washington.
A nor'easter is bringing powerful winds, local floods, and canceled events from the Mid-Atlantic
to New England, NPR's Ava Berger reports.
In Atlantic City, New Jersey, Talia Manno saw a car totaled from flooding on her street.
She said she hadn't seen so much water since Hurricane Sandy.
The water was just like you could literally see waves on my steps.
You could see waves on the steps.
That's how much water was there.
Jessica Lizboa was out on an Atlantic Ocean cruise as the storm grew.
It felt honestly like a rollercoaster.
An Olga Ostravetsky had planned to tie the knot on a beautiful fall day in September.
Instead, her small New York wedding continued, just with a lot more wind.
But it's kind of fitting, to be honest, because my fiancé and I met, and it was a torrential
downpour so we met in a day like this and we're also getting married on a day like this.
So flooding, heavy rain, and high winds are expected to continue to pummel the East Coast.
Several states have made emergency declarations.
Ava Berger, NPR News.
Control of the House is on the line in November, with both parties fighting over a relatively
small number of competitive districts.
One of those battles runs through Allentown, Pennsylvania, a majority Latino city.
NPR's Barbara Sprunt has the story.
Here in Allentown, worries about the economy and cost of living reign supreme.
Barbara Gonzales-Rizzotti sees the toll it takes as she runs a daycare.
Regardless of your political party or your ethnicity, we're all feeling the same things.
It's gotten to the point where there's almost, or we're gearing towards two classes of people,
the filthy rich or the dirt poor.
We're squeezing out the middle class.
Republicans made inroads with Latino voters in the 24 cycle, something they're trying
to replicate come November.
Barbara Sprunt, NPR News, Allentown, Pennsylvania.
House Democrats, meanwhile, are preparing a widespread agenda if their party takes back
control in November elections, including investigations of President Trump and members of his family.
You're listening to NPR.
Hollywood is riding an encore of Avengers Endgame to a surge in weekend attendance.
As NPR's Bob Mondello reports, superhero myths aren't the only ones proving to be durable
at the box office.
Avengers Endgame will have a brief burst of glory this weekend, wishing past $2.8 billion
worldwide, cementing its spot as the number two earner in box office history.
Tom Holland, one of its many stars, is also in Spider-Man Brand New Day, which is approaching
$2.5 billion worldwide in spot number three.
And he's also in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, a more traditional tale of mythic
heroes.
My dad is coming home.
Which recently passed $1.7 billion and still sells out many of its weekend IMAX performances
before it's through.
This old school sword and sandals epic with very few digital effects has a shot at cracking
the all-time worldwide top 10.
Bob Mondello, NPR News.
The band U2 surprised students at the Mount Temple Comprehensive School in Dublin, Ireland,
where it formed 50 years ago.
It flayed a seven-song set yesterday, including an encore of the song "With or Without You."
Lead singer Bono spoke to the students during the performance.
He reflected on the band's early days, and he also thanked the school and the community
for their support over the past several years.
The event was part of the promotion for U2's new album, "Carnival Deluse."
I'm Lynda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.
